Language barriers and mental health stigma further prevent them from seeking support. Settlement house staff are essential to the community, assisting older adults in navigating complex welfare systems, such as benefits enrollment and access to care. UNH is a long-time supporter of the Council’s Older Adults Mental Health Initiative, which makes mental health services accessible by putting them in community spaces where older adults already gather, such as senior centers, NORCs, and food pantries. It increases the capacity of CBOs serving older adults in identifying mental health needs, providing immediate mental health intervention, and referring clients to further psychiatric treatment when necessary. With recipients of this funding observing rising levels of social isolation, bereavement, and fear among immigrant populations, CBOs are able to meet their clients where they’re at, which is often in nonclinical settings like churches, which Chair Lee mentioned during questioning.
